He played [[college basketball]] for [[Southeast Missouri State University]]. He played in the [[NBA]] for the [[Dallas Mavericks]] and [[Atlanta Hawks]]. ==Early life== Cleveland was born in [[Memphis, Tennessee]], as the only child of mother Shonda Bowie.{{cite web |last=Singer |first=Trent |title=Former Southeast Missouri State men's basketball star Antonius Cleveland reflects on journey heading into NBA Summer League |url=https://www.semoball.com/story/2426065.html |website=SEMOBall |access-date=February 18, 2023 |date=July 6, 2017}} Bowie worked two jobs to support herself and Cleveland: as a nutrition supervisor for [[Memphis City Schools]] during the day and with [[FedEx]] during the night. Cleveland started his basketball career at [[Overton High School (Memphis, Tennessee)|Overton High School]] in Memphis for his freshman and sophomore seasons. He transferred to [[Germantown High School (Tennessee)|Germantown High School]] in nearby [[Germantown, Tennessee|Germantown]] for his junior season. Cleveland spent his senior year at Faith Baptist Christian Academy in [[Ludowici, Georgia]]. ==College career== Cleveland played for [[Southeast Missouri State University]] for four seasons, where he was the team's leading scorer in his junior (15.2 PPG; 10th in the conference) and senior (16.6 PPG; 7th in the conference) years.{{Cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/conferences/ovc/men/2016.html|title=2015-16 Men's Ohio Valley Conference Season Summary|website=College Basketball at Sports-Reference.com}}{{cite web |date=November 1, 2016 |title=Antonius Cleveland |url=https://semoredhawks.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/antonius-cleveland/7625 |access-date=July 28, 2024 |website=semoredhawks.com}} In his junior year he was also 5th in the conference with 1.6 steals per game, 9th with 6.6 rebounds per game, and 10th with a .437 field goal percentage. In his senior year he was also 3rd in the conference in steals per game (1.4), and 5th in field goal percentage (.543).{{Cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/conferences/ovc/men/2017.html|title=2016-17 Men's Ohio Valley Conference Season Summary|website=College Basketball at Sports-Reference.com}} He was selected to the All-[[Ohio Valley Conference]] (OVC) first-team in 2017.{{cite web |title=SEMO's Cleveland earns first-team All-OVC honors, Mahoney named Freshman of the Year |url=https://www.semoball.com/blogs/1909/entry/68426 |website=SEMOBall |access-date=February 17, 2023 |date=February 28, 2017}} ==Professional career== ===Dallas Mavericks (2017)=== After going undrafted in the [[2017 NBA draft]], Cleveland signed with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] to join their roster for the [[2017 NBA Summer League]]. While playing for [[Portland Trail Blazers|Portland]], he averaged 5.8 ppg in six games coming off the bench. On July 27, 2017, Cleveland signed with the Golden State Warriors on a training camp deal. On September 30, Cleveland was waived by the Warriors.{{cite news|last=Letourneau|first=Connor|title=Warriors waive Antonius Cleveland, Alex Hamilton|url=http://www.sfgate.com/warriors/article/Warriors-waive-Antonius-Cleveland-Alex-Hamilton-12244092.php|access-date=October 1, 2017|work=[[San Francisco Chronicle]]|date=September 30, 2017}} He was then assigned to the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]] [[NBA G League]] affiliate team on October 24, 2017. On November 17, 2017, Cleveland signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Dallas Mavericks]].{{Cite web |last=Sefko |first=Eddie |date=November 17, 2017 |title=Mavericks make it official with Antonius Cleveland, waive Gian Clavell |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/sports/mavericks/2017/11/17/mavericks-make-it-official-with-antonius-cleveland-waive-gian-clavell |access-date=July 28, 2024 |website=dallasnews.com}} He made his NBA debut later that night in a 111–87 blowout loss to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]], recording 2 points and 2 rebounds in 6 minutes of play.{{cite web|title=Butler, balanced Wolves pull away from Mavs for 111–87 win|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400974975|website=mavs.com|access-date=November 18, 2017|date=November 18, 2017}} Throughout his time on that two-way deal, he would split his playing time between the Mavericks and their G League affiliate, the [[Texas Legends]]. On December 18, 2017, he was injured in a 97–91 loss to the [[Phoenix Suns]]. He was waived from the team a day later, with his spot on the team being replaced by [[Kyle Collinsworth]].{{cite web|title=Mavericks sign Kyle Collinsworth to two-way contract|url=https://www.mavs.com/mavericks-sign-kyle-collinsworth-two-way-contract/|publisher=NBA|access-date=December 19, 2017|date=December 19, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171222052040/https://www.mavs.com/mavericks-sign-kyle-collinsworth-two-way-contract/|archive-date=December 22, 2017|url-status=dead}} ===Atlanta Hawks (2018)=== On February 22, 2018, the [[Atlanta Hawks]] signed Cleveland to a 10-day contract.{{cite news|title=Hawks Sign Antonius Cleveland To 10-Day Contract|url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-sign-antonius-cleveland-10-day-contract|access-date=February 22, 2018|publisher=NBA|date=February 22, 2018}} He signed his second 10-day contract with Atlanta on March 4. On March 14, 2018, Atlanta signed Cleveland to a multi-year contract.{{cite news |last=Wilson |first=Jaryd |date=March 14, 2018 |title=Hawks Sign Antonius Cleveland To Mult-Year Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-sign-antonius-cleveland-mult-year-contract |access-date=July 28, 2024 |publisher=NBA}} On July 21, 2018, Cleveland was placed on waivers by the Hawks.{{cite web |last=Bryant |first=Wayne |date=July 21, 2018 |title=Atlanta Hawks Request Waivers on Antonius Cleveland |url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/atlanta-hawks-request-waivers-antonius-cleveland @illawarrahawks' Antonius Cleveland locked up his opponents...|work=twitter.com/NBL|date=April 27, 2022|access-date=April 27, 2022}} ===Adelaide 36ers and Hapoel Eilat (2022–2023)=== On June 9, 2022, Cleveland signed a two-year deal with the [[Adelaide 36ers]].{{cite web|url=https://nbl.com.au/news/adelaide-add-antonius-cleveland-in-blockbuster-move|title=Adelaide Add Antonius Cleveland in Blockbuster Move|work=NBL.com.au|date=June 9, 2022|access-date=June 9, 2022}} He earned a second consecutive NBL Best Defensive Player Award for the [[2022–23 NBL season|2022–23 season]].{{cite web |last=Randall |first=Michael |title=NBA teams to circle as Sydney gun crowned MVP; winner named after shock snub: NBL Awards |url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/basketball/nbl/nbl-awards-2023-full-list-of-award-winners-xavier-cooks-nbl-mvp-sydney-kings-nominees-categories-latest-news/news-story/ee7734595a6caf8abbb9ae87268d74ca |website=Fox Sports |access-date=February 17, 2023 |date=February 7, 2023}} He parted ways with the 36ers after one season.{{cite web|url=https://nbl.com.au/news/36ers-release-cleveland|title=36ers release Cleveland|work=NBL.com.au|date=July 27, 2023|access-date=July 27, 2023}} On February 8, 2023, Cleveland signed a short-term deal with [[Hapoel Eilat B.C.|Hapoel Eilat]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League]], with an eye to returning to the NBL in 2024.{{cite web |last=Hudson |first=Jack |date=February 8, 2023 |title=Cleveland to play in Israel, return for NBL24 |url=https://www.adelaide36ers.com/news/cleveland-to-play-in-israel-return-for-nbl24 |access-date=February 17, 2023 |website=Adelaide 36ers}} ===Maccabi Tel Aviv (2023–2024)=== On July 27, 2023, Cleveland signed a two-year deal with [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League]].{{cite web|url=https://maccabi.co.il/news.asp?id=9689&lang=en|title=Maccabi adds Antonius Cleveland|work=maccabi.co.il|date=July 27, 2023|access-date=July 28, 2023}} He averaged 5.4 points and 1.7 rebounds per game during the 2023–24 season.{{cite web |title=Antonius Cleveland, Maccabi part ways after one year
